reason: The cited evidence (all from the same room-temperature salt spray study) supports premises 1–4 by describing the initial film, its protective role, chloride-induced rupture, and transition to iron oxide. However, premise 5, which is central to the hypothesis, is entirely unsupported: none of the cited passages involve high-temperature exposure (700–900 °C), thermal stresses, or enhanced chloride mobility at elevated temperatures.
premises: Q235 steel can be passivated to form a uniform, dense, dark black film
The passivation film provides electrochemical protection and limits early corrosion
Chloride ions cause passivation film rupture and localized corrosion
Film degradation transitions from passivation products to iron-oxide-based rust
High temperature (700–900 °C) accelerates chloride mobility and thermal stress-induced film embrittlement
